title: Concept Vector Effectiveness on Adversarially Fine-Tuned Unsafe Models

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear chain: if concept steering can recover safety in adversarially fine-tuned models, it is a lightweight recovery tool; if not, this documents an important limitation. Either outcome is highly informative for safety practice.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires performing adversarial fine-tuning (on harmful data) with varying severity, then attempting concept steering recovery. Adversarial fine-tuning requires careful setup to avoid producing genuinely dangerous artifacts. The fine-tuning itself requires more than beginner expertise.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple phases: adversarial fine-tuning at multiple severity levels, concept vector extraction from original model, recovery attempt, evaluation. Each phase is substantial. Exceeds 30 hours unless heavily simplified.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
